what_it_does: Solving SAT problems (Boolean satisfiability)—determining if a logical statement can be made true—is notoriously hard and grows exponentially with problem size. Traditional computer solvers slow down dramatically; hardware solvers exist but are limited to tiny problems. This paper uses a novel physics-inspired approach: it treats the logic puzzle like a system of coupled spinning magnets (a model from physics), implemented in a mixed-signal chip (part analog, part digital). The system runs continuously in analog time rather than stepping through digital logic, allowing massive parallelism. It can solve 50-variable, 218-clause 3-SAT problems with perfect reliability in just 31.7 microseconds—orders of magnitude faster than software approaches.
